source.text:
[Regulation (EU) 2021/697, Article 2, definition of 'legal entity'] ‘legal entity’ means a legal person created and recognised as such under Union, national or international law, which has legal personality and the capacity to act in its own name, exercise rights and be subject to obligations, or an entity which does not have legal personality as referred to in point (c) of Article 197(2) of the Financial Regulation;

[Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2018/1046 (the Financial Regulation that Regulation 2021/697 cites), Article 197(2)] 2. Any of the following applicants shall be eligible for participating in a call for proposals: (a) legal persons; (b) natural persons, in so far as this is required by the nature or characteristics of the action or the objective pursued by the applicant; (c) entities which do not have legal personality under the applicable national law, provided that their representatives have the capacity to undertake legal obligations on behalf of the entities and that the entities offer guarantees for the protection of the financial interests of the Union equivalent to those offered by legal persons.

rules.note: The associated countries are the EEA EFTA states (under the conditions of the EEA Agreement) and, since Regulation (EU) 2025/2653, Ukraine under the conditions of the EU-Ukraine Association Agreement. The EDF call documents of 2026 say: “Participation of entities established in Ukraine is pending the signature of the association agreement to EDF”, and we found no Official Journal text, Council decision or notice that says the EU-Ukraine association agreement applies to the EDF.

rules.note: A 'subcontractor' in the sense of this Regulation is narrower than any supplier: the definition in Article 2 requires at least 15 % of the value of the contract and a need for access to classified information, and leaves out suppliers that deliver components of their own design or production.
rules.reason: Common procurement under the Programme can include a subcontractor that is allocated between 15 % and 35 % of the value of the contract and is not established, or has no executive management structures, in the Union or an associated country, if a direct contractual relationship related to the defence product was established between the contractor and that subcontractor before the Regulation entered into force (it was published on 29 December 2025 and entered into force on the following day). This figure is a share of the contract value. It is not the 35 % component cost limit.

source.text:
[Regulation (EU) 2025/2643, Article 11(7)] By way of derogation from paragraph 6, in order to take into account industrial cooperation with non-associated third countries, common procurement that involves a subcontractor that is allocated between 15 % and 35 % of the value of the contract, and that is not established or does not have its executive management structures in the Union or in an associated country, shall be eligible for support under the Programme provided that a direct contractual relationship related to the defence product has been established between the contractor and that subcontractor prior to the date of entry into force of this Regulation.

[Regulation (EU) 2025/2643, Article 2, definition of 'subcontractor'] ‘subcontractor’ means an economic operator that is proposed by a candidate, tenderer or contractor to perform specific tasks or services under the supervision of the main contractor, contributing to the design or manufacturing of a defence product, other than what is provided by suppliers to implement the contract, for which it is allocated at least 15 % of the value of the contract, and that needs access to classified information for the performance of that contract; for the purposes of this definition, ‘supplier’ shall be understood as an economic operator that delivers components of its own design or production to the contractor.

rules.title: Subcontractors outside the Union: the 15 to 35 % allowance

rules.note: Derogation for subcontractors: see the information line on the 15-35 % subcontractor allowance below. The paragraph binds the contractor and the 'subcontractors involved in the common procurement' of Article 16(12), who provide critical inputs, are allocated at least 15 % of the contract value and need access to classified information. source.ref: Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1106, Article 16(3) and Article 16(12); Article 17 and the agreement with Canada (Decision (EU) 2026/1381, Agreement Article 5(2))
source.text:
[Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1106, Article 16(3), first sentence] Contractors and subcontractors involved in the common procurement shall be established and have their executive management structures in the Union, in an EEA EFTA State or in Ukraine.

[Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1106, Article 16(12)] For the purposes of this Article, ‘subcontractors involved in the common procurement’ means any legal entity which provides critical inputs that possess unique attributes essential for the functioning of a product, which is allocated at least 15 % of the value of the contract, and which needs access to classified information for the performance of the contract.

[Council Decision (EU) 2026/1381, recital (1)] was signed on 14 February 2026, subject to its conclusion at a later date, and has been applied on a provisional basis from 13 April 2026, pending its entry into force.

rules.note: Paragraph 8 also requires the infrastructure, facilities, assets and resources used for the procurement to be located in a Member State, an EEA EFTA state or Ukraine, with a narrow exception where no alternative is readily available. The paragraph binds the contractor and the 'subcontractors involved in the common procurement' of Article 16(12), who provide critical inputs, are allocated at least 15 % of the contract value and need access to classified information. A supplier below those thresholds is not bound by it.

source.text:
[Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1106, Article 16(3), first sentence] Contractors and subcontractors involved in the common procurement shall be established and have their executive management structures in the Union, in an EEA EFTA State or in Ukraine.

[Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1106, Article 16(12)] For the purposes of this Article, ‘subcontractors involved in the common procurement’ means any legal entity which provides critical inputs that possess unique attributes essential for the functioning of a product, which is allocated at least 15 % of the value of the contract, and which needs access to classified information for the performance of the contract.

[Council Decision (EU) 2026/1381, recital (1)] was signed on 14 February 2026, subject to its conclusion at a later date, and has been applied on a provisional basis from 13 April 2026, pending its entry into force.

issuers.notes: A new NCAGE request has to be justified by the need to catalogue a product bought by the Ministry of Defence, or by registration in the US System for Award Management (SAM). It is made through the catalogation body of the Army branch if the company has logged access to SICAD, otherwise through the NSPA NCAGE Code Request Tool (Ministry of Defence catalogation page, read on 20 October 2026). No fee is published, in line with NATO policy; the word 'gratuito' does not appear on the Spanish ministry page.

issuers.notes: The Spanish equivalent of AQAP is PECAL, audited through the structures of the Dirección General de Armamento y Material rather than a commercial certification body. On this route ISO 9001 from an ENAC-accredited body is a formal precondition, not only a practical one (DGAM procedure PA 4302); see the PECAL certification page.

steps.priceNote: In your country the state issues this itself, so the vendor price ranges in our sources do not apply and none is shown.
steps.summary: NATO quality assurance requirements for design, development and production. Not an eligibility condition of EDF, EDIP or SAFE: it enters through individual contracts and cascades down the supply chain.

issuers.name: Dirección General de Armamento y Material (DGAM), Ministerio de Defensa
issuers.notes: Initial audit by the DGAM; renewal and surveillance audits by certification bodies recognised by the CMDIN. The DGAM issues a quote for the fee; no amount is published.

steps.name: PECAL certification (Spain, DGAM)

neededFor.title: PECAL quality requirements come with the contract

steps.note: The chicken-and-egg of PECAL: the DGAM's initial audit expects a PECAL system audited by your management for at least nine months and at least one Ministry of Defence contract with PECAL requirements in the last two years (or a certificate of conformity signed by a DGAM quality representative). A newcomer therefore usually meets PECAL inside a first contract, under the quality representative's oversight, and applies for the certificate afterwards. It is not a block before a first contract: get the RID and ISO 9001 (or EN 9100) first.
